agent.problem: The card asks the baker to complete the unseen final word of the voice's line, “Do not call anything impure that God has made ___.” Even though clean is inferable, presenting the line itself up to its final word makes this a next-word completion exercise.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The baker must complete the angel's unseen statement with saved. The earlier cards establish that an angel appeared and that Peter was sent for, but they give no basis for choosing whether his message would save, warn or judge Cornelius's household.

agent.problem: Discovery questions recur beyond a few exceptions. Stop 1 cards 2, 7, 9 and 12, and stop 2 cards 3, 6 and 8, give little or no earlier-card basis for a reasoned pick: the baker must guess the initial reception, the sheet's contents, Peter's immediate response, the number of repetitions, whether he traveled alone, the angel's promised outcome and the comparison Peter recognized. This makes a substantial portion of the walkthrough depend on luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

human.problem: The wrong answers put sayings in the Lord's mouth that are altered or invented. 'Go and make disciples of all nations and baptize them in My name' changes Matthew 28:19. 'Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved on the last day' adds words to Mark 16:16. The docs say wrong answers are made up, and that Papa Dorin retells what Jesus said faithfully. They don't say whether a made-up wrong answer can be written as a saying of Jesus, or can change a real one.
human.question: Can wrong answers present invented or altered words as sayings of the Lord (Jesus or God)? Or must wrong answers for 'what did the Lord say' questions avoid looking like real Scripture?
